title: A turn that dies while minting an opencode session strands a server on its port
foundBy: session agent, investigating why the campaign project's opencode-fireworks smoke scenario is excluded from CI
details:
`cs-opencode-turn` booted a second opencode server to mint a session id. `mint_session` started `cs-opencode serve` on the derived port, waited for it, posted `/session`, killed it, then launched the TUI on the same port. Its only EXIT trap removed temp files, so a turn that died in that window left the transient server running.

Nothing cleared it afterwards. `cs-opencode-remote --kill` runs `tmux kill-session`, and the stranded server is not in a tmux session, so every later turn met it again.

Every guard then passed against the wrong server. Reproduced in a microVM: the stranded server answered `wait_healthy`, so the session was minted on it and bound to its own working directory, the sandbox user's home, rather than the one the turn asked for; `kill` reached only the driver's own unbound server; the 10s port-free loop fell through silently; the TUI then could not bind, yet `wait_healthy` and `session_known` both answered from the stranded server, so `ensure_session` returned 0 and the turn ran against a server no one could see. An agent whose file tools run in the wrong directory produces no reply, which reads from the host as a member that never started its turn.

A second opencode server also costs about 1 GiB. A member is given 2048 MiB, so a stranded server leaves little for the one doing the work.

notes.text: Removing the transient server exposed a second defect it had been hiding. The old mint ran `cd "$dir" 2>/dev/null || cd "$HOME"`, so a working directory that does not exist fell back silently. Binding the session to the directory explicitly made opencode honour it, and every prompt then failed with `FileSystem.realPath (/workspace) ENOENT`. cs-campaign asks every turn to run in /workspace, which a Firecracker member does not have. The driver now checks the directory and says which one it used.
